gaps.term: q divides no numerator or denominator
gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Presented as following from 'q must not divide xi', which constrains only denominators, and 'the finitely many matrices used' have not been introduced; the reader cannot see why numerators, or the entries of the factors F_1, F_2 and their inverses produced by elimination over Q, avoid q.

gaps.quote: To apply the shear, replace $D$ by $F_2D$ and $H$ by $F_1^{-1}H$.
gaps.note: The page uses F_1^{-1} and F_2^{-1} (and that Pi has rank M ones) but never says the factors are invertible; the terse elimination sketch does not say that clearing left entries is a column operation (right multiplication by a lower-triangular matrix), that pivots are scaled to 1, or how the operations assemble into F_1 and F_2.

gaps.term: why only the H update needs an interchange
gaps.quote: So the shear needs $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: The page never states the order of the H and D fields, so the reader cannot tell why D_tau <- D_tau + H_sigma (and D_tau <- H_sigma - D_tau) are linear-cost lower-triangular updates while H_sigma <- H_sigma + D_tau is not and needs an interchange.
